However, species cannot be verified from the landscape plan symbols, which show only generic tree circles labeled with category codes (M, PL, SYM) with no reference to the plant schedule species. comment: Compliance with transmission conductor clearance requirements cannot be verified because the voltage classification of the overhead electric line is not specified on any submitted plan. Per the grouping regulatory overview, transmission facilities are energized at 60kV or higher; most overhead facilities on typical development sites are distribution (less than 60kV). Without voltage documentation, it cannot be determined whether the 50-foot transmission clearance requirement applies. Additionally, tree species cannot be identified from landscape plan symbols (see EL-2.1). Applicant must provide: (1) voltage classification of the OHE line; (2) species identification keyed to landscape plan symbols; (3) measured clearance distances if transmission.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along OHE line

comment: Large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) may be proposed within 25 lateral feet of the overhead electric distribution conductor. The plant schedule (Sheet 35) lists species with sizes (Cedar Elm, Live Oak), but the landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not differentiate trees by size or mature height. Tree symbols on the landscape plan are shown only as generic circles with category labels (M, PL, SYM), with no notation of which trees are 'large' per ECM Appendix F standards. Measured clearance distances from conductor to tree trunks are also not provided. Applicant must provide: (1) identification of each tree symbol on landscape plan keyed to plant schedule; (2) mature height notation for each tree per ECM Appendix F; (3) measured clearance distances from outside conductor to tree trunk center for trees within 25 feet.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary and western areas near transformer pad

comment: Large trees (mature height 40+ feet) may be proposed within 50 lateral feet of overhead electric transmission conductor. comment: Trees are proposed throughout the site where underground electrical infrastructure (transformers, pull boxes, service lines) exists. Applicant must provide: (1) overlay of underground electric equipment locations (transformer pads, pull boxes) on landscape plan with coordinates; (2) measured clearance distances from each tree to nearest underground equipment; (3) verification that all trees maintain minimum 5-foot lateral clearance from underground equipment.

comment: Root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) are required for trees proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment. comment: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not identify the species of trees proposed near electric facilities. comment: Large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) are not differentiated on the landscape plan to allow verification of clearances from overhead electric facilities. The plant schedule on Sheet 35 lists mature heights (e.g., Cedar Elm, Live Oak specifications with container sizes indicating mature trees), but the landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not show these heights or indicate which tree symbols represent large trees. All tree symbols appear as identical generic circles with only category labels (M, PL), providing no visual differentiation of size. Without height notation on the landscape plan, reviewers and inspectors cannot identify which trees are subject to the stricter 25-foot (distribution) or 50-foot (transmission) large-tree clearance requirements. Applicant must provide: (1) notation of mature height on each tree symbol on landscape plan, or (2) distinct symbol types or colors to differentiate large trees (40+ feet) from other trees, or (3) clear legend showing which species in the plant schedule meet the large-tree threshold and marking those trees accordingly on the landscape plan.

comment: Tree clearance measurements are not dimensioned on the landscape plan, preventing evaluation of measurement reference points. The grouping's measurement methodology requires that clearances be measured from the outside conductor (not pole centerline), which can be 4+ feet offset from the pole center due to cross arms. Without clearance dimensions shown on the plan, it cannot be verified whether any measurements that may have been made used the correct reference point (outside conductor vs. pole center). This item can only be evaluated if clearance dimensions are provided on submitted plans. Applicant must provide: (1) clearance dimensions from tree trunks to outside conductor locations (not pole centerline) for any trees shown within 25 feet of electric conductors.
applicableAreas: Trees near overhead electric facilities

comment: Tree clearance measurements are not dimensioned on the landscape plan, preventing evaluation of tree reference points. This item can only be evaluated if clearance dimensions appear on submitted plans.
